record.title: Large Knowledge Model reports source-linked reasoning graphs and scientific retrieval gains
record.summary: A September 2026 preprint describes a scientific retrieval system that stores paper-level claims, premises, reasoning chains, conditions and source links, then connects them into question, workflow and evidence views. The authors report nearly twice as many known supporting and contradicting evidence pairs retrieved on SciFact-Open, a 5-point citation-F1 improvement from adding reasoning graphs over the same retrieved papers, and gains on three fixed-model scientific QA benchmarks. The reported evaluations are author-run; omission errors, independent reproduction and direct evaluation of the landscape’s evidence categorization remain open.
organizations: Institute of Theoretical Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors describe extracting papers into source-linked claims, inference factors, ordered reasoning chains, study settings and weak points, then organizing them into question, workflow and evidence views with incremental identity-preserving updates.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On SciFact-Open at a 50-paper budget, the paper reports 818 known-positive claim-paper pairs retrieved versus 443 for the released retriever, with recall rising from 39.38% to 72.71%. The pooled reference set includes judge- and MultiVerS-admitted candidate positives; original human annotations take precedence.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On two ScholarQABench subsets, adding reasoning graphs to the same retrieved papers, reranker and writing budget raises citation F1 by 5.3 and 5.1 percentage points, respectively, in the paper’s matched comparison.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: With GPT-5.4 fixed as the answer model, the paper reports LKM retrieval accuracy gains of 9.3, 4.2 and 14.7 points over no retrieval on ChemBench, PubMedQA and SciBench. The paper reports no paired confidence intervals for these point estimates.

evidence_gaps.description: The paper’s 100-paper extraction audit estimates hallucination but does not measure omitted claims/evidence; no independent audit or reproduction was performed.

The paper says the question/workflow/evidence landscape views and Evidence Engine categorization are not directly evaluated; the 1.4-billion-claim scale and service latency are author-reported production statistics.

brief.importance_rationale: If the matched retrieval and citation results generalize, persistent source-linked reasoning graphs could materially change scientific retrieval and evidence synthesis. A 6 reflects the tested system contribution while separating it from unverified production-scale figures and unmeasured omission/categorization errors.
limitations: The author preprint is under review and its experimental results are not independently reproduced here.
The extraction audit samples 100 papers and measures hallucination but not omission; the authors note figure, table and equation evidence may be incompletely captured.
Question/workflow/evidence landscape categorization is not directly evaluated in the paper.
The reported 1.4-billion-claim production scale and 740-ms median latency are author-reported and vary with a continuously updated service snapshot.
The evidence-discovery pooled reference set adds judge- and MultiVerS-admitted pairs; QA point estimates do not include paired confidence intervals.
organizations: Institute of Theoretical Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
brief.summary: A September 2026 preprint describes a scientific retrieval system that stores paper-level claims, premises, reasoning chains, conditions and source links, then connects them into question, workflow and evidence views. The authors report nearly twice as many known supporting and contradicting evidence pairs retrieved on SciFact-Open, a 5-point citation-F1 improvement from adding reasoning graphs over the same retrieved papers, and gains on three fixed-model scientific QA benchmarks. The reported evaluations are author-run; omission errors, independent reproduction and direct evaluation of the landscape’s evidence categorization remain open.

technical.claimed_result: The preprint reports nearly doubled known-positive evidence pairs on SciFact-Open, +5.3/+5.1 citation-F1 points from graph reasoning on two ScholarQABench subsets, and +9.3/+4.2/+14.7 QA points on ChemBench/PubMedQA/SciBench over no retrieval.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper reports benchmark results under described fixed budgets and a matched graph ablation. These results remain author claims and have not been independently replicated in this activation.
technical.mechanism: Papers are parsed into source-linked reasoning objects (questions, claims, premises, inference factors, ordered chains, settings and weak points). Typed links support hybrid retrieval and navigation from a conclusion to its evidence and source; cross-paper views organize questions, workflows and evidence.
technical.regime: Author-run deployed service; SciFact-Open 279 claims, 50 papers per claim; ScholarQABench 100 and 108 questions; ChemBench n=2,785, PubMedQA n=500 and SciBench n=580.
technical.reproducibility: Paper documents procedures and provides a public API description; no independent API trial, frozen corpus access or reproduction was performed.
technical.strongest_baseline: Released SciFact-Open retriever at 50 papers; same retrieved candidates/reranker/writer budget without reasoning graphs on ScholarQABench; no-retrieval condition with GPT-5.4 fixed on three QA benchmarks.

brief.title: Large Knowledge Model reports source-linked reasoning graphs and scientific retrieval gains
brief.why_it_matters: The work tests a shift from retrieving passages to retrieving structured claims together with how they were supported and under what conditions. If its reported gains hold under independent evaluation, this could improve evidence tracing and reuse in scientific research systems; current results do not establish that the full production-scale knowledge base is complete or self-correcting.
